# ==== Load/memory-read: 61 curated ====
#
# Rule applied: any InsKey with a WRITE-role destination operand (per the already-curated
# IOInfo.sm_75.txt) is VARIABLE:WRITE -- confirmed directly for LDG/LDC/LDL/TEX/SULD by real
# disassembled sm_75 control codes (TestData/CuTest/cudatest.7.sm_75.cuasm), extended by family
# analogy to ATOM/ATOMG/QSPC/LDSM/LD/TLD/TLD4/TXD/TXQ/ULDC, whose destination-bearing shape is
# solid even where IOInfo's own leading-predicate role guess for that same InsKey is not (the
# barrier-type call doesn't depend on which token the destination is, only that one exists).
# CCTL/CCTL_ARI have zero WRITE-role operands (confirmed empty/address-only IOInfo entries) --
# no operand for a barrier to protect, hence FIXED. RED_ARI_R/RED_AURI_R have an address plus an
# asynchronously-consumed source value but no destination -- structurally a store, not a load,
# hence VARIABLE:READ. See Reports/tasks.md Phase 1.1.

# ==== Store: 16 curated ====
#
# All VARIABLE:READ -- protects the source value register still being consumed asynchronously by
# the memory write (WAR case). Confirmed directly for STG/STL by real disassembled sm_75 control
# codes (STL [R1], R2 -> R0 in TestData/CuTest/cudatest.7.sm_75.cuasm); STS/ST/SUST follow by
# family analogy (same address+value shape, no destination). See Reports/tasks.md Phase 1.1.

STG_ARI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # confirmed: "STG.E.SYS [R18], R3 ;" -> R1 in real sm_75 control codes  # e.g. "STG.E.128.SYS [R4], R12 ;"
STG_ARURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STG.E.SYS [R2.64+UR6], R7 ;"
STG_AURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STG.E.SYS [UR4], R0 ;"
STL_ARI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # confirmed: "STL [R1], R2 ;" -> R0 in real sm_75 control codes  # e.g. "STL.64 [R1], R10 ;"
STL_ARURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STL [R6+UR5+0x4], R19 ;"
STL_AURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STL [UR6], RZ ;"
STS_AI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "@!P1 STS [0x5000], R63 ;"
STS_ARI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STS.128 [R8.X16], R4 ;"
STS_ARURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STS.64 [R95+UR7], R88 ;"
STS_AURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STS.128 [UR5], R8 ;"
ST_ARI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "ST.E.SYS [R2], R0 ;"
ST_ARURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "ST.E.U8.STRONG.GPU [R34.64+UR4+0x20], R22 ;"
ST_AURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "ST.E.128.STRONG.GPU [UR4+0x200], R4 ;"
SUST_ARI_R_II_II: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "SUST.D.BA.2D.STRONG.CTA.TRAP [R4], R2, 0x0, 0x5c ;"
SUST_ARI_R_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "SUST.D.BA.1D_ARRAY.U16.STRONG.CTA [R22], R7, R0 ;"
SUST_ARI_R_UR_II: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "SUST.D.BA.1D_ARRAY.U16.STRONG.CTA [R14], R7, UR16, 0x0 ;"

# ==== Control-flow: 36 curated ====
#
# All FIXED (no scoreboard barrier). Confirmed directly by real disassembled sm_75 control codes
# for BAR/BMOV/BRA/BSSY/BSYNC/CALL/DEPBAR/EXIT/RET (TestData/CuTest/cudatest.7.sm_75.cuasm --
# every occurrence shows no read/write barrier set, only the wait-mask field is ever used, which
# this table doesn't model). The rest of the bucket is the same kind of op -- branch-unit control
# flow, thread-block/warp barriers, or B-register convergence-barrier bookkeeping -- none of which
# write a value via the async memory/SFU pipe the 6 scoreboard slots protect, so FIXED follows by
# direct architectural consistency with the confirmed entries, not a guess. This also resolves the
# 3 InsKeys IOInfo.sm_75.txt still flags as operand-role guesses (B2R_R_P/BAR_II_P/BREAK_P_B) --
# their *latency* classification doesn't depend on what their uncertain operand's role turns out
# to be. See Reports/tasks.md Phase 1.1.

B2R_R: FIXED  # e.g. "B2R.RESULT R11 ;"
B2R_R_P: FIXED  # e.g. "B2R.RESULT RZ, P0 ;"
BAR_II: FIXED  # confirmed: "BAR.SYNC 0x0 ;" sets no barrier in real sm_75 control codes  # e.g. "BAR.SYNC 0x0 ;"
BAR_II_P: FIXED  # e.g. "BAR.RED.AND 0x0, P0 ;"
BAR_R: FIXED  # e.g. "BAR.SYNC R0 ;"
BAR_R_R: FIXED  # e.g. "BAR.SYNC R6, R6 ;"
BMOV_B_L: FIXED  # confirmed: "BMOV.32 B15, MACTIVE ;" sets no barrier in real sm_75 control codes  # e.g. "BMOV.32 B15, MACTIVE ;"
BMOV_B_R: FIXED  # e.g. "BMOV.32 B6, R16 ;"
BMOV_L_B: FIXED  # e.g. "BMOV.32.PQUAD MACTIVE, B15 ;"
BMOV_R_B: FIXED  # e.g. "BMOV.32.CLEAR RZ, B0 ;"
BPT_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BPT.TRAP 0x1 ;"
BRA_II: FIXED  # confirmed: 11 real sm_75 BRA occurrences, none set a barrier  # e.g. "BRA 0xe0;"
BRA_P_II: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P1 BRA !P2, 0x7b0 ;"
BREAK_B: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P0 BREAK B0 ;"
BREAK_P_B: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P0 BREAK P2, B2 ;"
BRXU_UR_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BRXU UR8 -0x5570 ;"
BRX_R_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BRX R14 -0x390 ;"
BSSY_B_II: FIXED  # confirmed: "BSSY B0, 0x9d0 ;" sets no barrier in real sm_75 control codes  # e.g. "BSSY B0, 0x9d0 ;"
BSYNC_B: FIXED  # confirmed: "BSYNC B1 ;" sets no barrier in real sm_75 control codes  # e.g. "BSYNC B1 ;"
CALL_II: FIXED  # confirmed: real sm_75 CALL occurrences set no barrier  # e.g. "CALL.REL.NOINC 0x1c0 ;"
CALL_R: FIXED  # e.g. "CALL.ABS.NOINC R12 ;"
CALL_R_II: FIXED  # e.g. "CALL.REL.NOINC R8 0x0 ;"
DEPBAR_SB_II: FIXED  # confirmed: "DEPBAR.LE SB5, 0x1 ;" sets no barrier in real sm_75 control codes -- DEPBAR consumes/waits on an existing barrier, it doesn't set one  # e.g. "DEPBAR.LE SB5, 0x1 ;"
DEPBAR_SB_II_SBSET: FIXED  # e.g. "DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0, {4,3,2,1} ;"
ERRBAR: FIXED  # e.g. "ERRBAR;"
EXIT: FIXED  # confirmed: 8 real sm_75 EXIT occurrences, none set a barrier  # e.g. "@P0 EXIT ;"
EXIT_P: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P0 EXIT P1 ;"
LEPC_R: FIXED  # writes a deterministic PC value, not memory/SFU-pipe data  # e.g. "LEPC R32 ;"
MEMBAR: FIXED  # e.g. "MEMBAR.SC.CTA ;"
NANOSLEEP_II: FIXED  # e.g. "NANOSLEEP.WARP 0xf4240 ;"
NANOSLEEP_R: FIXED  # e.g. "NANOSLEEP.WARP R0 ;"
NOP: FIXED  # e.g. "NOP;"
RET_R_II: FIXED  # confirmed: 7 real sm_75 RET occurrences, none set a barrier  # e.g. "RET.REL.NODEC R2 0x0 ;"
WARPSYNC_II: FIXED  # e.g. "WARPSYNC 0xffffffff ;"
WARPSYNC_R: FIXED  # e.g. "WARPSYNC R34 ;"
YIELD: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P0 YIELD ;"

# ==== Tensor-core (MMA): 3 curated ====
#
# All VARIABLE:WRITE -- tensor-core MMA ops are well-documented (CUTLASS docs, NVIDIA
# architecture whitepapers, latency-hiding guidance) as high, multi-cycle-latency ops the compiler
# must interleave with independent work; no real sm_75 MMA sample was in reach to confirm the
# exact barrier bit directly, but every other destination-producing op observed in this table's
# real evidence sets a write barrier, and tensor cores are a canonical textbook example of an
# op needing one. See Reports/tasks.md Phase 1.1.

BMMA_R_R_R_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "BMMA.88128.XOR.POPC R22, R4.ROW, R26.COL, R18 ;"
HMMA_R_R_R_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "HMMA.1688.F16 R2, R20, R24.reuse, R2 ;"
IMMA_R_R_R_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "IMMA.8816.S8.S8.SAT R2, R68.ROW, R72.reuse.COL, R2 ;"

# All VARIABLE:WRITE. Confirmed directly for SHFL by a real disassembled sm_75 control code

# family -- they run through the same cross-lane permute/reduction network as SHFL -- so the
# classification extends by structural analogy, not direct per-opcode confirmation.

MATCH_R_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "MATCH.ANY R7, R13 ;"
